quote: In the past the man has been first; in the future the system must be first.
note: This one sentence is the 20th-century factory.

quote: 47 tons per man per day, in place of 12 and a half tons
note: ×3.8 the output for +61% pay. Who keeps the difference?

replies.text: Taylor's own figure is "60 per cent. higher wages", so your maths is right. His answer is that the gain is shared between workman, company and buyers; he doesn't give a split. Also: this story is Taylor's retelling, and historians (Wrege and Perroni, 1974) have argued it was tidied up. I put that caution in section 5.

replies.text: Fair reading. It was also used against him at the time: the 1911–12 House committee hearings on the Taylor system were partly about how workers were treated. I didn't add this to the note; say if you want it there.
